title: Rust in Practice
summary: Build real Rust: custom iterators, modules, error handling, collections, trees, pattern matching, a tokenizer and a cache.
description: You know the language; now put it to work. Each lesson is a small, complete piece of the kind of code Rust programmers write every day: an iterator of your own, a tidy module with private parts, errors that explain themselves, a linked list built from Option<Box<Node>>, a generic stack and queue, a binary search tree, an expression evaluator built on pattern matching, a tokenizer driven by a state machine, and a least-recently-used cache.
outcomes: Build Rust iterators, collections, a tokenizer and a cache.
